entries.en: We don't know if she's involved but it might be a good idea to try and find her. See what she knows. Her name's Liara. Dr. Liara T'Soni.
It's your decision, Commander. You're a Spectre now. You don't answer to us.
But your actions still reflect on humanity as a whole. You make a mess and I get stuck cleaning it up.
Glad to hear it, Commander. Remember: you were a human long before you were a Spectre.
Not exactly the answer I was looking for, Shepard. Remember: you were a human long before you were a Spectre.
I have a meeting to get to. Captain Anderson can answer any questions you might have.
Between the visions and your warnings about the Reapers, the Council's starting to think you're a little unstable.
I think you get results. As long as you keep getting the job done, there's nothing to worry about.
I have. Just make sure you keep getting results and we won't have a problem.
It's not personal, Shepard. Just keep getting results and they'll leave you alone.
This isn't right! The Normandy belongs to you!
I want the truth. Why are you stepping down, sir?
Come clean with me, Captain. You owe me that much.
Does this have to do with Saren keeping you out of the Spectres?
I won't let you down, sir.
Saren's not going to get away this time.
I'll take good care of her, sir.
What kind of leads do we have?
The Reapers are the real threat.
The colonists on Feros might still be alive.
Sounds like we should head for the Artemis Tau cluster.
Maybe I can get to Noveria before the geth.
I'll try not to make things any harder on you, Ambassador.
I'll take care of Saren. You take care of the political fallout.
Tell them not to worry.
How many more times do I have to prove myself before they start to listen to me?
I'm out to stop Saren. Nothing else matters.
I would've saved the colony if I could've. But stopping Saren is more important.
You don't give a damn about the colonists. It's all just politics to you, isn't it?
Making your day, Ambassador. She has information linking Saren to the geth.
You wanted proof Saren's a traitor. This is it.
This quarian can help us bring down Saren. I would've told you that if you hadn't jumped down my throat.
What kinds of things do you look for?
Tell us what you found.
Where's the proof you promised?
What kind of evidence did you find? How did you get it?
What did you find out?
Saren won't get out of this one.
The vision on Eden Prime -- I understand it now. I saw the Protheans being wiped out by the Reapers.
They won't believe you anyway. Just keep them out of this.
The Reapers are a threat to every species in Citadel space. We have to tell them.
This is a lot to handle. They might just ignore everything we tell them.
Forced retirement?
There's more to this.
Because of Saren?
Saren will pay.
Any word on Saren?
What about the Reapers?
Count on me.
I'll start with Feros.
I'll start there.
I'm going to Noveria.
I'll be careful.
It might be necessary.
That's your job.
They were expendable.
I did my best.
That's all you care about?
They've learned.
She can help us.
Please, continue.
What about Saren?
Something of value?
And what did you find?
We've got him!
She's right.
It's not far-fetched.
It's true.
Don't tell them.
They need to know.
Will they believe it?
You could be useful.
You saw me in the alley, Commander. You know what I can do. Let me come with you.
That's Saren's voice. This proves he was involved in the attack!
The Conduit must have something to do with the beacon. Maybe it's some kind of Prothean technology... like a weapon.
Wait... there's more. Saren wasn't working alone.
I don't recognize that other voice. The one talking about Reapers.
He said Eden Prime brought him one step closer to finding the Conduit. Any idea what that means?
Are they some kind of new alien species?
I feel like I've heard that name before...
What's the Conduit?
Reapers? What are they?
Reapers? Sounds familiar.
The mission on Eden Prime was a chance to prove you could get the job done. Instead, Nihlus ended up dead and the beacon was destroyed!
Saren's a threat to every human colony out there. He needs to be stopped. The Council has to listen to us!
I'm not going to sit on my ass just because the Council doesn't want to do anything. If they won't stop Saren, I will.
He's dangerous.
They're blind.
We have reports she was exploring an archeological dig on one of the uncharted worlds in the Artemis Tau cluster.
Pleased greeting. Human, it is always good to see your kind.
Modestly, I work to bring the problems and the requests of the elcor groups to the attention of the Council.
Ha. They only give us these positions to keep us quiet. The Council doesn't care about our races.
Chastising rebuke, your tone is inappropriate, Din. This human is not to blame for your malcontent or your misconceived suspicions.
Our people communicate less through words and more through scent and slight movements.
Plainly, we discovered our vocal expression was not enough to convey the feelings of our conversations to other species.
Why do you bother, Calyn? These Earth-clan don't really care about our ways.
Remorseful response, Din. You don't truly believe that. And if you do, I am very sorry for you.
Sincere farewell. Good day to you, human. Enjoy your time on the Citadel.
Surprised greeting, human Spectre. Sincere congratulations, word has arrived of your induction.
Surprised welcome, you have returned, human. Genuine inquiry, what may I do for you this day?
Pleasant greeting, it is good to see you again, human Spectre. Sincere query, how may I help you this day?
Why do you explain what you're about to say?
Goodbye, Ambassador.
Genuine enthusiasm, I delight in telling the history of my people. It is agreeable to share our culture with others.
The elcor were just beginning to explore Council space when the asari first made contact with us.
With their help, we discovered the relay closest to our system and from there, the Citadel.
Proudly, within one lifetime we established a regular route to the Citadel and quickly became one of the more active species living on this great station.
Frankly, we elcor prefer the safety and familiarity of our own colonies to the confines of space travel.
Our society is built on small tight-knit groups, though we are always welcoming to outsiders.
Our government tends to be very stable. Our people are not very comfortable with sudden changes.
Tell me more about your species.
Tell me about the history and origins of the elcor.
I'd like to know more about the culture of the elcor.
History
Culture
I am Ambassador Calyn. Genuine query, is there something I can do for you this day?
Nothing, thanks.
I understand what you are saying, but these allegations are very serious. I can't just--
This is serious. My reputation is at stake. I spoke with the Consort in confidence, and her alone. And she betrayed that confidence.
All right. I will look into it for you. In the meantime, do not do anything rash.
Earth-clan, you are in the wrong place, I think. Your ambassador is next door in the large office.
I look out for the best interests of the volus people. No easy task considering how often we are overlooked by the Council.
Chastising rebuke, Din. The Council favors your species greatly.
You are naïve. The Earth-clan will be invited to the Council long before our species will.
All species must prove themselves before they join the Council. All but the Earth-clans, it would seem.
Dismissive, ignore the volus ambassador, human. He is incorrect in his assessment.
Really? How long have we been waiting? How long do you think we'll continue to wait? Bah. This talk is wasted on the humans.
You are in the embassy for the volus and the elcor.
In this shared space, I aid my fellow volus. When I'm not being interrupted.
Yes, yes. Good day, Earth-clan.
Well, the new Earth-clan Spectre. Obviously, you are already lost. Your ambassador is next door.
Ah, the Earth-clan again. What is it now?
The Earth-clan Spectre has returned to speak with me.
What is it you do here?
Why aren't the elcor or volus part of the Council?
I'm sure our history and culture would bore you, Earth-clan.
My people came to the Citadel shortly after the asari and salarians had discovered it. We were instrumental in establishing a standardized galactic economy.
However, despite our long association with the Citadel and our many contributions to galactic society, we still do not hold a seat on the Council.
We are tribal by nature, but our ways are not violent. We barter and trade our lands and tribe members in order to increase status.
Larger tribes often engulf smaller ones and eventually split again. Our society is very malleable, and our government is always shifting and changing.
Since we're not physically adept, we trade our services for protection.
You humans are new to the Citadel, and yet the Council has granted you great favor.
Chastising rebuke, Din. Your species has always been granted many concessions. Volus territory has expanded ten-fold since coming to the Citadel.
I'd like to know more about the volus.
Actually, I would like to know more about your history.
Tell me about volus culture.
You seem to have a bit of a chip on your shoulder, Din.
Why so cranky?
Embassy
Council admittance.
